_readme: EXAMPLE: RAK4631 (Android, LiPo) sensor. Not read by the service; copy from here.
1. Copy the block under "devices" into the "devices" object of server/python/devices.json.
2. Replace the devEUI key (lowercase, 16 hex chars) with your sensor's, and change name and ntfy_topic.
3. "family" must be the ChirpStack device-profile name: RAK4631 (aliases android, custom also work).
4. application_id is the ChirpStack application UUID, needed only for downlinks; the service also
learns it from the first uplink. Secrets stay as ${ENV_VAR} placeholders.
5. Save devices.json: it is hot-reloaded, no restart. The settings below are pushed on the next uplink.
Everything except name and family is optional; the type's defaults fill the gaps.
tk_correction_c is subtracted from the raw temperature (8 C for this hardware), then compared with temp_alarm_min_c (and temp_alarm_max_c, temp_alarm_hysteresis_c).
circuit_mode event: the firmware sends one frame when the contact opens and nothing on close, so each pulse
is a fire-only alarm (pulses within circuit_hold_s count as one) and there is no 'cleared' message.
motion_min_detections 3 + motion_window_s 30: alarm only on 3 detections within 30 s (1 = every detection).
frequency 10 means 10 Hz; for RAK4631 it is sent as register code 47. Hz, wire codes and code:N all work.
notify_fire / notify_clear are keyed by alarm kind (temp_low, temp_high, battery_low, battery_empty, motion, circuit, tilt, stale).
TWO DEVICES: settings shared by every RAK4631 live once under "families"; sensor3 and sensor4 only
list what is theirs. sensor4 is the minimal case plus two overrides (freezer limit, every motion alarms).
Precedence, later wins: the type's built-in defaults, "defaults", "families", the device entry.
Note: a dict such as notify_fire is replaced as a whole by a lower layer, not merged key by key.
application_id is set per device (not in "families"): devices of one type can sit in different ChirpStack applications.
